HatchPattern__Hardcore__Meta.Meta__Description: Hardcore in section - angular broken stones, loosely packed, with a few small pieces between them. Much coarser than the concrete above it, which is the point: the slab and what it sits on must read apart.
HatchPattern__Hardcore__Meta.Meta__WhyPaperUnits: Every length here is PAPER millimetres, like the dash patterns in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json, so the hatch measures the same on the sheet at 1:20 and at 1:100. Pattern scale adjusts from there.
HatchPattern__Hardcore__Meta.Meta__WhyScatter: The positions are a blue-noise scatter, generated ONCE and written in below as fixed numbers, so screen and paper can never disagree. It was scored on a torus - the gap across a tile seam counts like any other gap - and against the regularities that survive a repeat: two marks sharing a column (an endless vertical line once the tile repeats) or a row. A lattice was never an option: it lays visible stripes across a wall.
HatchPattern__Hardcore__Meta.Meta__WhyInsideTheTile: Every mark sits wholly inside the tile, so nothing crosses a seam at all: a browser clips a <pattern> at its tile edge and the PDF stamper does not.

HatchPattern__Hardcore__Identity.Identity__Description: How this pattern is named, found and grouped in the pattern lists.
HatchPattern__Hardcore__Identity.Identity__Note: Compacted hardcore and granular sub-base under a slab.

HatchPattern__Hardcore__Tile.Tile__Description: The repeating cell, in paper millimetres.
HatchPattern__Hardcore__Tile.Tile__Note: Eight stones and six small pieces. Not square, so the repeat does not line up on the diagonal.

HatchPattern__Hardcore__Defaults.Defaults__Description: What the pattern draws with until a use sets its own. The stroke is 0.35 pt (0.1235 mm) at scale 1 and grows with the pattern scale; a line weight typed in the panel does not. 'inherit' takes the colour of whatever carries the hatch - a vector's edge colour - until a pattern colour is picked.

HatchPattern__Hardcore__Glyphs.Glyphs__Description: Drawn about the glyph's own origin, y pointing DOWN, in tile millimetres. Strokes only: the PDF stamps a tile as lines and never fills one.

StoneA.Glyph__Note: Angular, never rounded: hardcore is broken, not dug.

StoneC.Glyph__Note: Six sided and flatter, lying down.

Pebble.Glyph__Note: Fills the gaps between the stones, as the fines do on site.

HatchPattern__Hardcore__Bounds.Bounds__Description: How far a use may scale and turn this pattern before it stops reading as the material.
